segments.caption: Every house quote in India starts with one formula.
segments.vo: Every house quote in India starts with one formula.

segments.caption: Built-up area, times a rate per square foot.
segments.vo: Built-up area, times a rate per square foot.

segments.caption: 1,000 sq ft, at ₹2,500 a square foot. ₹25 lakh.
segments.vo: A thousand square feet, at two thousand five hundred rupees a square foot. Twenty-five lakh.

segments.caption: Basic homes are often quoted around ₹1,800 to ₹2,300 a square foot.

segments.caption: Leak one is hiding in the word area.

segments.caption: Contractors usually quote on built-up area: every floor, including the walls, the balcony and the staircase.
segments.vo: Contractors usually quote on built-up area: every floor, including the walls, the balcony and the staircase.

segments.caption: But you live in carpet area, the floor you can actually walk on. And it's always smaller.

segments.caption: Leak three is the soil.

segments.caption: Across north Karnataka, a lot of land sits on black cotton soil. It swells when it's wet and shrinks when it's dry.
segments.vo: Across north Karnataka, a lot of land sits on black cotton soil. It swells when it's wet and shrinks when it's dry.

segments.caption: Build on it like normal ground, and you get cracks. Build on it properly, and the foundation costs more.

segments.caption: Nobody hides anything. The quote is just vague.

segments.caption: Your quote says cement. But which cement? 33, 43 or 53 grade? OPC or PPC?
segments.vo: Your quote says cement. But which cement? Thirty-three, forty-three or fifty-three grade? O P C or P P C?

segments.caption: PPC is usually a little cheaper per bag, and both are fine when used right.
segments.vo: P P C is usually a little cheaper per bag, and both are fine when used right.

segments.caption: Your quote says steel. But which TMT? Fe 500 or 500D? Which brand?
